narrative.title: Why Hsiang Is Studying Artificial Intelligence
narrative.summary: Hsiang views AI as a generational inflection point comparable to the dawn of personal computing — a foundational shift that will inevitably reshape every industry and workflow.
details: She sees today's AI transition as comparable to when computers were first introduced to the world: it is not a temporary trend, and organizations and engineers will inevitably need to build with it.

Rather than remaining a passive consumer of AI tools, she enrolled in the Master of Artificial Intelligence at the University of Auckland to build rigorous theoretical foundations alongside her 9+ years of production engineering.

She pairs academic study with hands-on systems engineering — already designing and running a self-hosted distributed workflow automation and AI agent platform (n8n, OpenClaw, Docker, Redis, PostgreSQL).

narrative.title: Long-Term Vision: Evolving Internal AI Systems into Enterprise Platforms
narrative.summary: Long-term, Hsiang aims to lead and evolve internal AI tooling into reliable, secure, enterprise-grade systems integrated with core business operations.
details: Her long-term goal is to take internal AI prototypes and automation workflows and evolve them into production-ready enterprise platforms — complete with reliability, security best practices, observability, CI/CD, and clean integration with existing backend systems.

Many enterprise AI initiatives stall between proof-of-concept and production because of architecture, data integrity, compliance, and legacy integration challenges — the exact problems she has solved for 9+ years across core banking migrations and large-scale fintech platforms.

Combining senior C#/.NET backend architecture, a Master of Management in Accounting, and a Master of Artificial Intelligence positions her to bridge executive business goals with durable, scalable AI infrastructure.

narrative.title: Engineering & Leadership Approach
narrative.summary: Pragmatic, quality-driven senior engineer focused on maintainability, security, TDD, CI/CD, and pragmatic mentorship.
details: Believes software should align tightly with real business and financial outcomes, not just technical elegance.
Advocates for strong engineering fundamentals — xUnit/TDD, TeamCity CI/CD pipelines, thorough code reviews, and security best practices.
Enjoys mentoring teammates, unblocking complex legacy/validation issues, and translating ambiguous stakeholder requirements into clear technical deliverables.
